notes.title: Under a Desert Sun: Seekers of the Cursed Vessel - Beta 3.31 Patch Notes
notes.notes:
Another day another set of small fixes!
Additions

Added voice acting for Anpu character.

Used writing tech in intros for a more cinematic feel.

Bugfixes

Fixed an issue where conversation audio was also being muted during menu and conversation moments, causing voice acting and menu clicks to not be loud enough.



Thanks so much for the feedback all!

Raymond

notes.title: Under a Desert Sun: Seekers of the Cursed Vessel - Beta 3.30 Patch Notes
notes.notes:
Some small improvements today!

Improvements

Tutorials now use a cueing system so they do not overlap.

Added a small note that tells the player when they’ve reached the (demo) level cap.

Fixed some dust shaders that did not have full transparency as intended — dust in collapsing caves looks good again.

Kind regards,
Raymond

notes.title: Under a Desert Sun: Seekers of the Cursed Vessel - Beta 3.29 Patch Notes
notes.notes:
Improvements

In-game menus (settings, skills, ledger, etc.) can now be exited with B (East button) on gamepads.

Added voice acting tracks for Soldier intro (Adventurer voice tracks pending).

Bugfixes

Fixed an issue where sound bars could accidentally be set to 100% when clicking a nearby setting button.



Thank you to all players of the demo so far! I’ve been able to fix many smaller things these past few days thanks to your feedback. Deeply appreciate everyone trying the demo — and if you have feedback, don’t forget to join the Discord for that and the latest news!



Kind regards,

Raymond

notes.title: Under a Desert Sun: Seekers of the Cursed Vessel - Beta 3.27 Patch Notes
notes.notes:
Hi there, 

Another day another round of improvements. These are focussed on the soundsystem and general settings.

Improvements

Overhauled sound system and sound settings system, providing better control over player sound, ambient sound, and music sound volumes.

Made sure you can reach settings in the main game menu (previously only changeable in the start game area).

Bugfixes

Some sound effects were not taken into account by the SoundManager and would be unaffected by volume changes. All sounds should now be accounted for.

Fixed an issue where the game would sometimes lose track of the FPS counter, preventing it from being turned on or off.



Kind regards,

Raymond

notes.title: Under a Desert Sun: Seekers of the Cursed Vessel - Beta 3.23 Patch Notes
notes.notes:
Bugfixes

Fix for footstepping tech sometimes leaving behind a few steps.

Fix for ghost soldiers getting hit by player hits.

Fix for small lighting issue in some dungeons.

Fix for conversation starting too early in special weapon temple.

Removed some old ladder climbing code that could interfere.

Class Tweaks

Toned down Adventurer melee damage increase per level.

Improvements

Added more spawn areas for Nazi enemies surrounding the Nazi base to keep things active.

Added more torches on some paths to make it easier to follow during night.

notes.title: Under a Desert Sun: October Early Access Release October – Join Us at Next Fest!
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

I’m hard at work getting the demo ready for Steam Next Fest, and things are coming along nicely. The plan is to have a solid, playable chunk ready before the event—and then open up Early Access shortly after.

Here’s a look at what’s been happening behind the scenes:


Elemental effects now hit harder (and look cooler)[previewyoutube="XvNYjR8uigM;full"][/previewyoutube]
Elemental damage now packs more punch. Burning enemies like mages ignite immediately, and frozen foes will shatter into satisfying icy shards when smashed. Combat just got a whole lot juicier.


Dual wield skill is finalized and fully working[previewyoutube="540v9Umq9Fg;full"][/previewyoutube]

One of the trickiest parts of our skill system is ensuring different abilities and elemental effects can combine seamlessly. Dual wielding posed a unique challenge—it affects how the player attacks, reloads, and triggers other effects. After a lot of tweaking and accounting for edge cases, it’s now working neatly with all elemental builds.


Main quest progression and new boss: the Flamethrower Baddy[previewyoutube="z3O028wojoU;full"][/previewyoutube]

Development on the main quest continues, bringing new story content and fresh enemies—like this brand-new boss wielding a brutal flamethrower. The footage is from an early test map, but… you get the point. WOOSH.


New enemy tech and UI polish[previewyoutube="6sNk8syuW3g;full"][/previewyoutube]

I’ve also expanded general enemy behavior, adding projectile-throwing types to keep you on your toes. On top of that, the enemy name UI and various visual polish passes make everything look sharper and feel more refined.


Destructible environments (with loot!)[previewyoutube="r_o0UvIZ_DE;full"][/previewyoutube]

Destructibles are in! Blowing things up is always fun, but they also help make the world feel alive—and sometimes they drop loot too. This is a small taste of the broader loot system that’s planned for expansion after the Early Access release.


Optional lore system: readable tomes and books[previewyoutube="kdooV0LbUZc;full"][/previewyoutube]

For players who love world-building, I’ve added a system for reading tomes, scrolls, and ancient books. It’s completely optional, but offers rich lore if you want to dig deeper. And yes—it already looks pretty neat!


Major progress on the main story (but no spoilers)
The largest additions are actually in the main quest and story… but I’m deliberately showing less of that for now. If you’re part of the Discord, you may have seen a few extra glimpses. For everyone else: it’s shaping up to be something special.


👉 Don’t forget to wishlist Under a Desert Sun: Seekers of the Cursed Vessel
It really helps with visibility and keeps you in the loop for Early Access and Next Fest!
🎮 Want to see more and join the community?
Hop into the Discord and chat with fellow adventurers, give feedback, or just lurk for sneak peeks.

notes.title: Under a Desert Sun: Seekers of the Cursed Vessel - progression update
notes.notes:
Hello Seekers,

I thought it was a good moment to highlight some fresh progress! Development continues at full speed, starting with new environments and further work on the main quest. As some of you in the Discord already know, I use the main quest as a way to push myself to build new systems. I'm now at the point where everything leading up to the final moments of the main quest is functional—both tech-wise and, for the most part, art-wise.

That means it was time to move the story forward again, which in turn forced me to create new areas, enemies, and gameplay features. One such feature is an improved day and night system, with smoother lighting transitions and smarter particle effects that fade out instead of abruptly disappearing. Below you'll find a quick idea of the new day/night features and a few in-editor screenshots showing the early stages of these new zones.


[previewyoutube="W8fBpR4LRIY;full"][/previewyoutube]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/98681fabc5451329fa38a12406b8b82819de5a14.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/d4345efc8b2f50bf2f8ad3fd06a0145ef4d8c1ac.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/fc8caccf66faf6037f19803c5d2e466e21a1f55d.png"]

Creating these new areas also meant designing new enemy types—specifically ones that shoot projectiles! From Nazis who fire bullets to arcane mummies casting magical bolts, I needed to build the underlying tech. To get that going, I set up a test using our trusty mummy as a prototype. This allowed me to develop the full system: bullets, shooting and casting animations, and proper hit detection.


[previewyoutube="UoC7sk9P1rg;full"][/previewyoutube]
Naturally, new areas also bring more destructibles. And let’s be honest—breaking stuff in an ARPG is just fun. (As you can see from me thrashing around... purely professional testing, of course 😏)


[previewyoutube="r_o0UvIZ_DE;full"][/previewyoutube]
On the technical side, Steam Deck optimization remains a major goal. The game currently runs at a stable 45 FPS on Deck without any upscaling like FSR—so you get a clean image and native visuals. To get there, I’ve upgraded several systems under the hood. Particle systems now fade naturally, enemy spawning uses pooled and distance-aware logic, and we've improved object occlusion and visibility handling to keep things smooth when off-screen. These changes help across all platforms but especially make the Deck experience strong.
[hr][/hr]
Join the Discord for daily development discussions and behind-the-scenes previews.
And if you like what you see—wishlist the game on Steam to support the journey!

notes.title: Performance Update
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/0dbb010153a6582344408a76138adebabfd291d6.gif

Performance is key in a game like this. The Steam Deck is a prime target for testing, and beta revealed that enemies’ individual search-and-behavior loops were impacting performance. A full AI overhaul merged those cycles under a single “Mother” controller (yes, a nod to Alien’s onboard computer), unlocking (as you can see in the small vid above):

A stable 45 FPS on Deck—no FSR or other upscalers needed

Dramatically reduced CPU load during the wildest firefights

Rock-steady frame pacing even in the most demanding areas

Cracking this “Mother” system feels like mastering the more difficult parts of gamedesign. It is a truly proud achievement that brings the project right on target for Deck performance. More polish is coming—stay tuned!

notes.title: Developer Update: Skill System Progress
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/7e15d0657de73b13dc6d425c1a7b26fe49a1ce14.gif
Hi everyone! I’ve been working on further developing the skill system for the two playable classes currently in Under a Desert Sun: Seekers of the Cursed Vessel.

The goal is to give players meaningful choices through a layered approach to character customization:

On the right side of the screen, you'll find a classic Diablo II-style skill tree—both in appearance and philosophy. It’s deliberately old-school: no free respecs, so each decision matters and helps shape a distinct build.

Complementing that is a more flexible card slot system, which lets you adjust your playstyle on the fly. These cards introduce powerful modifiers and unique mechanics that can significantly alter your approach to combat and exploration.

The interaction between the two systems should create exciting variety. For example, one skill card available to the Adventurer disables rifle usage but unlocks the ability to dual wield pistols, enabling faster, close-range aggression.

The footage included in this update shows the player selecting a Frost or Burn bullet skill card—activating elemental bullets that apply freezing or burning effects to enemies on hit. This is just one of many ways skill cards can evolve your character’s abilities.
